newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hariri forms his third Lebanon government.
newsitem.headline: Hariri forms his third Lebanon government.

text.p: Lebanon's Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri formed a new 30-member government on Thursday including 12 new ministers but retaining all the top ministers of his outgoing cabinet.
Hisham al-Shahar, director-general of the cabinet, announced the new government totalling the same number of ministers as the outgoing team.
The cabinet was the third Hariri has formed since becoming prime minister in October 1992 with a mandate to rebuild Lebanon from the ruins of the 1975-90 civil war.
Top ministers in the outgoing team including interior, finance, economy, defence and foreign affairs were unchanged, Shahar said.

Hariri retained the finance ministry which he held in the previous government. His close colleague Fouad Siniora retained the ministry of state for financial affairs in which he has acted as finance minister in Hariri's previous two governments.

However, Hariri also took control of the Posts and Communications Ministry previously held by Al-Fadel Chalaq, another close colleague and a dynamic minister who was dropped after 18 months in office.
The 12 new ministers included several politicians viewed as potential enemies or rivals of Hariri, despite repeated statements by Hariri that he wanted a homogeneous team free of internal disputes.
They were Sleiman Franjieh (Health), Talal Arslane (Emigrants), Akram Chehayeb (Environment).

Political sources said parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, who has been a rival of Hariri in the past, had increased his influence in the government through the appointment of two members of his Amal movement and one supporter.
Druze leader Walid Jumblatt, who has recently criticised Hariri, also increased the number of members of his Progressive Socialist Party (PSP) in the cabinet from one to two.
Announcement of the government followed nearly two weeks of negotiations between Hariri, Berri and President Elias Hrawi as they sought to increase their influence in the cabinet.
